claims.text: Exacerbation not responding to glucocorticoids: plasma exchange (any relapsing form; not primary progressive MS)
claims.quote: If glucocorticoids are ineffective in reducing the severity of an exacerbation, plasma exchange may be used (4). Plasma exchange can be used for any relapsing form of MS (relapsing-remitting, progressive relapsing, secondary progressive), but is not used for primary progressive MS.

claims.text: Vitamin D supplements (eg, 600 to 4000 IU/day) generally recommended; mixed evidence they may delay progression;
claims.quote: Vitamin D supplements (eg, 600 to 4000 IU/day to achieve blood levels of 20 to 50 ng/mL [50 to 125 nmol/L]) are generally recommended based on mixed evidence that they may delay the risk of disease progression
Serum vitamin D levels should be monitored to make sure that dosing is adequate.
Vitamin D also reduces the risk of osteoporosis, particularly in patients at increased risk because of decreased mobility or glucocorticoid therapy.
